beats.say: NASA just shared Hubble photos of nine galaxies acting as giant magnifying glasses.
Here is the trick. Mass warps space, and light passing a heavy galaxy curves with it.
So light from a galaxy far behind gets steered around the one in front, toward us.
We see that hidden galaxy smeared into bright arcs, sometimes doubled.
Line them up perfectly, and the light makes a full circle, an Einstein ring.
Slightly off, and one galaxy shows up four times in the same image.
The more mass, the stronger the bend. So the bending weighs the lens, including invisible dark matter.
Tiny kinks in the arcs could even expose small clumps of dark matter.
A survey at Kitt Peak spotted these lenses. Hubble zoomed in. And Roman, launched in August, will find many more.
